title: The Book of Life
definition: The Book of Life is Scripture's image of God's secure knowledge of those who belong to Him and inherit eternal life.
summary: The Book of Life speaks of God's certain knowledge and secure record of those who belong to Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lamb whose people are recorded as His redeemed ones.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine points to divine security, final judgment, and belonging to the Lamb. The names of the redeemed are not kept by human memory or religious reputation but by God Himself. It reminds believers that final acceptance rests with the Lord who knows His own.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people fear being forgotten, rejected, or erased by earthly powers. The Book of Life teaches that God's record is decisive. It also warns that eternal destiny is not determined by outward appearance but by belonging to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rejoice that the Lord knows those who are His. Let the seriousness of final judgment stir evangelism and self-examination. Find comfort in God's faithfulness rather than in public recognition.
